title: Thomason comparison for lax and oplax Grothendieck constructions
statement:
Use the simplicial replacements $\mathrm{BK},\mathrm{KB}$ of [lem-coef-bousfield-kan-comparison-calculus] and weak homotopy equivalences of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For a small category $C$ and a diagram $F:C\to\mathrm{Cat}$ of small categories define two categories $\operatorname{Th}_C F$ and $\operatorname{Gr}_C F$, both with objects $(c,z)$, $z\in F(c)$. In $\operatorname{Th}_C F$ a morphism $(c,z)\to(c',z')$ is a pair $a:c\to c'$, $b:F(a)z\to z'$. In $\operatorname{Gr}_C F$ it is a pair $a:c'\to c$, $b:z\to F(a)z'$. Identities and composition use the corresponding functors $F(a)$ and composition in the fibers. Write $NE$ for the nerve of a category $E$, whose $r$-simplices are strings of $r$ composable arrows, with composition/deletion faces and identity-insertion degeneracies. There are natural weak homotopy equivalences
$$\mathrm{BK}_C(NF)\longrightarrow N\operatorname{Th}_C F,\qquad
\mathrm{KB}_C(NF)\longrightarrow N\operatorname{Gr}_C F.$$
They are natural under natural transformations of diagrams and reindexing functors and send a degree-zero pair $(c,z)$ to that same object. In particular, if $F\to G$ is a natural transformation such that every $NF(c)\to NG(c)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, the induced functors $\operatorname{Th}_C F\to\operatorname{Th}_C G$ and $\operatorname{Gr}_C F\to\operatorname{Gr}_C G$ induce weak homotopy equivalences on nerves.

source.place: Zhen Lin Low, Revisiting function complexes and simplicial localisation (2014), Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6, pp. 5–6; last assertion is the immediate naturality and Lemma 1.3 consequence. No Stacks tag states this homotopical result.

proof.text: Put $E=\operatorname{Th}_CF$ and let $\pi:E\to C$ send $(c,z)$ to $c$. Write a simplex of $\mathrm{BK}_C(NF)$ as a base chain $c_0\xrightarrow{a_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{a_r}c_r$ and a fiber chain $z_0\xrightarrow{b_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{b_r}z_r$ in $F(c_0)$. If $a_{ij}:c_i\to c_j$ is the composite, define $\tau_F$ to be the chain in $E$ with vertices $(c_i,F(a_{0i})z_i)$ and $i$th arrow $(a_i,F(a_{0i})b_i)$. This has the required source because $F(a_i)F(a_{0,i-1})=F(a_{0i})$. Internal faces compose both arrows and the equality $F(a_{0,i+1})(b_{i+1}b_i)=F(a_{0,i+1})b_{i+1}\,F(a_{0,i+1})b_i$ gives the corresponding composite in $E$; the first face transports the remaining fiber chain by $F(a_1)$, exactly the first-face formula for $\mathrm{BK}$, and the last face simply deletes the last vertex. Inserting identities gives the degeneracy identities. Thus this formula defines the required simplicial comparison map, before asserting it is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Low, Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6, pp. 5–6: agent-supplied comma-resolution proof of the stated theorem; the source states the theorem without a proof.

proof.text: For each $c\in C$ form the category $D(c)=(\pi\downarrow c)$. Its objects are $(e=(d,z),u:d\to c)$, and a morphism $(e,u)\to(e',u')$ is $v:e\to e'$ with $u'\pi(v)=u$. Postcomposition in $u$ defines a strict functor $D:C\to\mathrm{Cat}$. Define $R_c:D(c)\to F(c)$ by $R_c(e,u)=F(u)z$. On $v=(f,b)$ it is $F(u')b$, using $u'f=u$. These $R_c$ are strictly natural in $c$. The inclusion $J_c:F(c)\to D(c)$ sends $z$ to $((c,z),1_c)$; then $R_cJ_c=1$ and the arrows $(u,1):(e,u)\to J_cR_c(e,u)$ give a natural transformation $1\to J_cR_c$. Thus $P=R_c$ and $Q=J_c$ satisfy $PQ=\mathrm{id}_{F(c)}$ (a zigzag of length zero) and there is a natural transformation $\mathrm{id}_{D(c)}\Rightarrow QP$; no component need be invertible. By [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence], $|NR_c|$ and $|NJ_c|$ are inverse up to continuous homotopy and $NR_c$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Its weak homotopy equivalences (bijection on path components and isomorphisms of all homotopy groups at all basepoints of the realization) are literally those of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

source.place: Low, Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6, pp. 5–6: agent-supplied comma-resolution proof of the stated theorem; the source states the theorem without a proof.

proof.text: Define a bisimplicial set $B_{p,q}=\coprod_{c_0\to\cdots\to c_p}ND(c_0)_q$. Horizontal first faces use postcomposition $D(c_0)\to D(c_1)$, other horizontal faces compose/delete base arrows, and degeneracies insert identities; vertical operators are those of the nerve. They commute because postcomposition is a functor. Thus $\operatorname{diag}B=\mathrm{BK}_C(ND)$. The natural transformation $NR:ND\to NF$ of Step 2 induces $r=\mathrm{BK}_C(NR):\operatorname{diag}B\to\mathrm{BK}_C(NF)$. By the objectwise invariance assertion of [lem-coef-bousfield-kan-comparison-calculus], $r$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. All categories and coproducts here are small because $C$ and all $F(c)$ are small.

source.place: Low, Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6, pp. 5–6: agent-supplied comma-resolution proof of the stated theorem; the source states the theorem without a proof.

proof.text: Forget the arrows to $c_0$ in a vertical comma-category chain to obtain an augmentation $v:B\to\operatorname{const}_{\mathrm{horizontal}}NE$. It is compatible with horizontal operators because postcomposition changes only those arrows. For fixed $q$, a vertical comma chain is determined by a chain $e_0\to\cdots\to e_q$ in $E$ and the arrow $u_q:\pi(e_q)\to c_0$: the other arrows are $u_i=u_q\pi(e_i\to e_q)$. Consequently the horizontal simplicial set $B_{\bullet,q}$ is the disjoint union, over $NE_q$, of the nerves $N(\pi(e_q)\downarrow C)$. Each undercategory has initial object $1_{\pi(e_q)}$. Let $P$ be the functor from the undercategory to the terminal category $[0]$ and $Q$ the functor picking the initial object. Then $PQ=\mathrm{id}_{[0]}$, and the unique arrows from the initial object form a natural transformation $QP\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}$. By [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence] the map of its nerve to $\Delta^0=N[0]$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, in the sense of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Realization of a disjoint union is the disjoint union of realizations: in the quotient defining realization all relations retain the summand index. Components and based homotopy groups of a disjoint union are computed in the summand containing the basepoint. It follows that $B_{\bullet,q}\to NE_q$, with the target constant in the horizontal direction, is a weak homotopy equivalence, also when $NE_q$ is empty. The exchanged-directions assertion of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] now implies that $v:\operatorname{diag}B\to NE$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Low, Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6, pp. 5–6: agent-supplied comma-resolution proof of the stated theorem; the source states the theorem without a proof.

proof.text: The maps $v$ and $\tau_Fr$ are simplicially homotopic; the homotopy must be checked, rather than identifying these two maps. In a diagonal $r$-simplex of $B$, write its vertical chain as $e_i=(d_i,z_i)$ with comma arrows $u_i:d_i\to c_0$. The vertices of $v$ are $e_i$, whereas those of $\tau_Fr$ are $w_i=(c_i,F(a_{0i}u_i)z_i)$. There are arrows $\eta_i=(a_{0i}u_i,1):e_i\to w_i$. The comma equation $u_i=u_{i+1}\pi(e_i\to e_{i+1})$ makes the square with the $i$th arrows of the two chains commute: both composites have base map $a_{0,i+1}u_i$ and fiber map obtained by applying $F(a_{0,i+1}u_{i+1})$ to the fiber map of $e_i\to e_{i+1}$. For each order-preserving $t:[r]\to[1]$, select $e_i$ when $t(i)=0$ and $w_i$ when $t(i)=1$, using their own chain arrows within a block and the commuting square for the possible mixed arrow. These chains define $H:\operatorname{diag}B\times\Delta^1\to NE$. Restriction to any subsequence commutes with the construction: if the first retained base index is $j$, postcomposition replaces $u_i$ by $a_{0j}u_i$, and $a_{ji}a_{0j}u_i=a_{0i}u_i$ leaves $w_i$ and $\eta_i$ unchanged. Repeated vertices likewise insert identity arrows. This verifies all simplicial operators and gives endpoints $v$ and $\tau_Fr$. Writing $A=\operatorname{diag}B$, the cylinder theorem gives the continuous homotopy $h:[0,1]\times|A|\to|NE|$ defined by $h(t,x)=|H|(\rho_A^{-1}(x,t))$. By [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change], the realized homotopy gives the same component function and identifies the homotopy-group maps by the basepoint-change isomorphism along $t\mapsto h(t,x)$ for each source point $x$. Thus $\tau_Fr$ is a weak homotopy equivalence because $v$ is. Since $r$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, two-of-three (or cancellation of the resulting bijections and group isomorphisms) proves that $\tau_F$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Low, Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6, pp. 5–6: agent-supplied comma-resolution proof of the stated theorem; the source states the theorem without a proof.

proof.text: For a simplicial set $X$ write $X^{\mathrm{op}}_n=X_n$ with the order of faces and degeneracies reversed: $d_i^{\mathrm{op}}=d_{n-i}$ and $s_i^{\mathrm{op}}=s_{n-i}$. Reversing coordinates defines a natural homeomorphism $|X^{\mathrm{op}}|\to|X|$, $[x,(t_0,\ldots,t_n)]\mapsto[x,(t_n,\ldots,t_0)]$: a face inserts a zero and a degeneracy adds adjacent coordinates, so their reversed versions respect exactly the quotient relations; the same formula is a continuous inverse. It follows directly from the definition of weak homotopy equivalence that taking opposite preserves and reflects it. Reversing nerve chains gives $N(A^{\mathrm{op}})\cong(NA)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Put $F^{\mathrm{op}}(c)=F(c)^{\mathrm{op}}$. From the displayed morphism definitions, $\operatorname{Gr}_CF\cong(\operatorname{Th}_C F^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}$: a reversed Thomason arrow is precisely $a:c'\to c$, $b:z\to F(a)z'$. Reversing the base chain and the fiber chain in the degreewise formula of [lem-coef-bousfield-kan-comparison-calculus] gives $\mathrm{KB}_C(NF)\cong(\mathrm{BK}_C(NF^{\mathrm{op}}))^{\mathrm{op}}$; endpoint faces are interchanged and the interior compositions and identity insertions agree. Conjugating $(\tau_{F^{\mathrm{op}}})^{\mathrm{op}}$ by these isomorphisms produces the desired weak homotopy equivalence $\mathrm{KB}_C(NF)\to N\operatorname{Gr}_CF$. This is a direct dualization of the already proved comparison, with no assumption that the two Grothendieck categories are equivalent.

source.place: Low, Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6, pp. 5–6: agent-supplied comma-resolution proof of the stated theorem; the source states the theorem without a proof.

proof.text: A natural transformation $\phi:F\to G$ sends $(c,z)$ to $(c,\phi_cz)$ and sends the two kinds of fiber arrows by $\phi$. In the formula for $\tau$, its naturality equation $\phi_{c_i}F(a_{0i})=G(a_{0i})\phi_{c_0}$ gives equality of every vertex and arrow in the two composite chains. A reindexing functor $h:C'\to C$ sends the base chain to its image under $h$ and each composite $a_{ij}$ to $h(a_{ij})$, giving the same equality for $Fh$. The degreewise functoriality of $\mathrm{BK},\mathrm{KB}$ in [lem-coef-bousfield-kan-comparison-calculus] identifies these with the stated comparison squares. Chain reversal and coordinate reversal commute with these maps, so the oplax comparison has the same naturality. In degree zero $a_{00}=1$, and hence both comparisons send the summand element $(c,z)$ to the identical object $(c,z)$.

source.place: Low, Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6, pp. 5–6: agent-supplied comma-resolution proof of the stated theorem; the source states the theorem without a proof.

proof.text: Finally, let $\phi:F\to G$ be objectwise a weak homotopy equivalence on nerves. Objectwise invariance of [lem-coef-bousfield-kan-comparison-calculus] makes the corresponding $\mathrm{BK}$ and $\mathrm{KB}$ maps weak homotopy equivalences. In each naturality square of Step 7 the horizontal comparison maps are weak homotopy equivalences by Steps 5 and 6. Therefore the map on Grothendieck nerves is a weak homotopy equivalence by two-of-three, using exactly the definition/model weak equivalences of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. This proves the final clause without assuming that $\phi_c$ is an equivalence of categories.
